newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha tumbles on crudes, European markets.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha tumbles on crudes, European markets.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices fell sharply on Thursday, weighed down by an overnight crude loss as well as easier European naphtha markets, traders said.
They also said that petrochemical firm Showa Denko's announcement of a 10-percent cut in ethylene production had little impact on the market.

Open-spec naphtha for first-half July was bid at $207.50 per tonne, while offers were quoted at $209.00. On Wednesday, one first-half July contract was traded betweem a Japanese trading house and a European trader at $212.25, and another one changed hands at $212.00.
In physical naphtha trading, a petrochemical firm said it bought one spot cargo to be delivered to Chiba, near Tokyo, in the second half of June at around the mean of Japanese quotes minus $1.50.
On Tuesday, another spot cargo to be delivered to Chiba in the latter half of June was sold to a refiner at slightly lower than the mean of Japanese quotes minus $1.50.

Showa Denko announced that it plans to cut its ethylene output by 10 percent at its 730,000-tonne-per-year plant in southern Japan in the second and third quarters this year to cool Asia's naphtha market.
